items.meaning: dissect; cut open for anatomical study
items.reviewNote: Disséquons describes anatomical study of insects. The I disséqua_anatomical plan and all three questions, plus VI disséqué, were read. The present plural surface shares that planned French verb meaning; no tense-only sense is created. All plural verbs accept le, while opening the body for study differs from drawing, feeding or release.

items.meaning: flies; flying insects
items.reviewNote: Mouches are actual insects dissected by the philosophers, not decorative beauty patches. The global insect meaning, its complete three-band singular bank and the exact plural patches bank were read. Add the plural surface on the existing proper mouche noun insect sense. Mouches/araignées/chenilles/limaces are feminine plural nouns; flying and buzzing distinguish the target without a grammar filter or biological claim about the narrative specimens.

items.meaning: measure; determine dimensions
items.reviewNote: Mesurons des lignes determines geometric lengths. The VI measured-dimensions bank was re-read in all three bands; share that planned French mesurer verb and meaning, without a present-tense-only identity. Every verb takes les and nous; determining dimensions differs from weighing, drawing or moving.

items.meaning: lines; geometric figures with length but no breadth
items.reviewNote: Lignes names geometric one-dimensional objects studied by measurement, not lines of prose or a family lineage. No global or earlier proper ligne family exists. Lignes/surfaces/sphères/masses are feminine plural nouns in des; the explicit one-dimensional clue excludes surfaces, spheres and masses without implying all lines are straight.

items.meaning: assemble; combine together
items.reviewNote: Assemblons des nombres describes combining numbers in arithmetic. No global or earlier assembler verb exists. Prepare the ordinary bringing-together meaning rather than a special arithmetic-only lemma. All four plural verbs take les; bringing elements together differs from separation, erasure or disregard.

items.meaning: numbers; numerical quantities
items.reviewNote: Nombres are abstract numerical quantities used in arithmetic. The earlier II nombre_count meaning and its three questions were read. Share its proper French noun and quantity meaning, with conceptual scope reconciliation of counted and abstract numbers before import rather than a plural-only sense. Nombres/coloris/contours/poids are masculine plural nouns, including the invariant plural spellings; numerical values rather than color, outline or weight select nombres.

items.meaning: points; matters or questions under discussion
items.reviewNote: Deux ou trois points refers to matters understood by the philosophers, not tiny instants, opportune moments or negation point. The global point noun and adverb owners and earlier II point_tiny_instant plan were read. Prepare the discussion-topic meaning under the existing proper noun owner. Points/lieux/moments/trous are masculine plural nouns; the stated subjects of debate exclude spatial places, time and physical holes.

items.meaning: understand; grasp the meaning
items.reviewNote: Both entendons mean understanding philosophical points, once positively and once under n’…pas. The global hear and intend senses and the VI understanding bank were read in all bands. Share the planned understanding meaning under entendre, with no polarity-, object- or tense-only sense. All four plural verbs accept les; grasping meaning differs from forgetting, hiding or distorting.

items.meaning: came over someone; arose as an urge
items.reviewNote: Il prit fantaisie aux deux visiteurs is the onset of a spontaneous desire to question the philosophers. The exact earlier VII prend-onset bank and all three questions were read, with Académie 1762 envie/fantaisie evidence. Share that same proper prendre verb meaning; the separate prit la parole occurrence is a whole idiom. All choices are grammatical verb labels in a quoted-construction prompt, and onset rather than passing, lack or persistence selects prit.

items.meaning: fancy; a spontaneous desire or impulse
items.reviewNote: Prit fantaisie names the visitors’ sudden wish to question the humans. No global or earlier proper fantaisie noun exists. Académie 1762 directly records this spontaneous-desire construction. Fantaisie/certitude/nécessité/habitude are feminine singular nouns after une; a wish differs from knowledge, requirement or routine, without treating it as imagination of a nonexistent object.

items.meaning: question; ask someone for information
items.reviewNote: Interroger ces atomes pensants means asking the humans questions to learn their agreed knowledge. No global or earlier French interroger verb exists. Every infinitive takes the unchanged direct object les; asking for information differs from providing it, ignoring people or congratulating them. No interrogation-by-authorities-only sense or literal questioning of physical atoms is created.

items.meaning: things; matters or possibilities referred to
items.reviewNote: Choses refers to agreed matters in186 and possible realities in208; the214 le bout des choses span reuses the complete expression bank. The broad proper chose noun and its three physical-object questions were read. Add an abstract-reference bank on the same generic thing meaning, with scope reconciliation before import; neither abstractness nor plurality alone creates a second generic sense. Choses/personnes/localités/dates are feminine plural nouns; the clue explicitly excludes persons, places and dates.

items.meaning: agreed; were in agreement
items.reviewNote: Les choses dont ils convenaient are matters on which the philosophers agreed. The global agree/settle meaning, its three questions and I conviendront_agree bank were read; exclude suitability convient. Add the imperfect plural surface on the same proper convenir agreement meaning. All four en predicates are viable; accepted agreement differs from doubt, ongoing debate or lying.

items.meaning: great; major or prominent
items.reviewNote: La grande étoile des Gémeaux identifies a prominent star in the narrator’s wording. The published importance/intensity/ampleur grand meaning and all three questions, plus VI physical-size grande bank, were read. Add an importance-context bank on that broad adjective sense, without independently asserting the star’s physical diameter or luminosity. All alternatives agree feminine singular; importance rather than smallness, secondary status or insignificance selects grande.

items.meaning: debate; argue about an issue
items.reviewNote: Nous disputons sur des points is the older debating construction, supported by the source contrast between agreed and disputed subjects. No global or earlier French disputer verb exists. Académie1762 records arguing questions on both sides with the non-pronominal construction. The authored independent retrieval sentence uses the modern pronominal form of the same arguing meaning under the proper disputer headword; final import must compare this construction without making a reflexive-only sense. Every plural predicate accepts nous nous; opposed arguments rather than agreement, silence or reconciliation select disputons. This is intellectual debate, not necessarily a physical fight.

items.meaning: degrees; units equal to one three-hundred-and-sixtieth of a full turn
items.reviewNote: Degrés measures angular separation between the named stars, not temperature or educational rank. No global or earlier French degré noun exists. Degrés/radians/tours/secteurs are masculine plural nouns; the exact fractional-turn definition distinguishes degrees from radians, full turns and sectors. The narrative angular amount is not independently verified by this vocabulary bank.

items.meaning: half; one half of the preceding unit
items.reviewNote: Et demi after degrés adds a half-degree. Académie9 sectionI explicitly classifies demi after et as an adjective agreeing in gender with the preceding unit and remaining singular. Do not import it as a nominal half-unit or create a separate half-degree-only sense. All alternatives are metalinguistic word labels rather than sentence substitutions; half rather than a quarter, third or tenth selects demi. No existing global or earlier demi owner exists.

items.meaning: half-diameters; radii
items.reviewNote: Demi-diamètres de la terre supplies the historical distance unit of Earth radii in the story. No global or earlier proper demi-diamètre noun exists. Demi-diamètres/diamètres/côtés/périmètres are masculine plural nouns; the center-to-edge half-diameter clue distinguishes radii without validating the narrative Earth–Moon ratio as a current astronomical fact.

items.meaning: weighs; has a specified weight
items.reviewNote: Both pèse ask or state the weight of air. The global moral-burden sense and IV pesaient_weighed bank were read in all three bands. Share the earlier planned physical-weight meaning under proper existing peser rather than moral pressure or a present-only new meaning. All four finite predicates fit the subject and a numerical complement; weight rather than price, content or count selects pèse. Source comparisons remain attributed narrative measurements.

items.meaning: air; the gaseous mixture around us
items.reviewNote: Votre air and l’air denote the physical atmospheric gas mixture whose weight is being discussed, not appearance or manner. The existing proper air noun and all appearance questions were read. Prepare the atmospheric meaning on that same lemma. Air/oxygène/azote/ozone are masculine singular vowel-initial nouns fitting l’; the mixture rather than a single constituent gas selects air, with no agreement or elision filter.

items.meaning: catch out; trick someone into an error
items.reviewNote: Il croyait les attraper means catching the philosophers out with a question, not grabbing a fleeing person or catching a chill. The published physical-trap, catching-person and cold meanings with their banks were read. Académie9 records figurative deceiving. Prepare the trick/catch-out meaning under the same proper attraper verb, with overlap review of trap language before import. Each infinitive takes les; inducing an error differs from information, reassurance or praise.

items.meaning: volume; the amount of space occupied
items.reviewNote: Un pareil volume compares equal spatial amounts of air and water. No global or earlier volume noun exists. Volume/périmètre/diamètre/poids are masculine singular nouns; three-dimensional occupied space differs from boundary length, a through-center length or weight. The later bound-book volume is a distinct meaning under this same proposed proper volume noun owner; do not create duplicate lemmas or validate the narrative density ratio.

items.meaning: volume; a complete bound book
items.reviewNote: Ce volume is the complete book the Sirian delivers, revealed as blank at the Academy, not a spatial measurement. Prepare the bound-book meaning under the single proposed proper volume noun owner also used for spatial extent; keep these two semantic meanings distinct. Volume/feuillet/paragraphe/chapitre are masculine singular nouns; a complete bound book differs from one leaf or textual subdivisions. No new lemma per homographic sense is allowed.

items.meaning: light; having little weight
items.reviewNote: La plus légère describes low weight for the water used in the story’s comparison. The global low-weight/agility adjective and all three questions were read. Add the feminine surface on the same physical low-weight meaning; adjective gender and superlative construction do not create a fresh sense. All alternatives agree feminine singular. This explains the narrator’s comparison without asserting a special kind of scientifically verified lightest water.

items.meaning: nineteen; ten plus nine
items.reviewNote: Dix-neuf is the numerical multiplier in the stated air-to-gold comparison. No global or earlier French dix-neuf family exists. All four numerical expressions fit the arithmetic prompt; the sum determines nineteen. The bank does not validate nineteen thousand as an actual physical density ratio or create a context-only arithmetic identity.

items.meaning: ducat; an old coin, commonly made of gold
items.reviewNote: L’or de ducat refers to gold associated with the historical coin. No global or earlier French ducat noun exists. Académie9 records an old coin, usually gold and sometimes silver, with value varying by place. Ducat/lingot/bracelet/chandelier are masculine singular nouns; being a coin rather than a block of metal, jewelry or a lighting object selects ducat. No modern conversion price, fixed gold purity or country-exclusive meaning is asserted.

items.meaning: answers; replies to questions
items.reviewNote: Réponses names the philosophers’ replies to the giants’ measurement questions. No global or earlier proper réponse noun exists; the répondre verb cannot own the noun. Réponses/questions/hésitations/demandes are feminine plural nouns after des. Replies supplying requested information differ from asking, hesitation or requesting, with no noun-agreement filter.

items.meaning: tempted; inclined to do something
items.reviewNote: Fut tenté de prendre les philosophes pour des sorciers expresses an inclination, not an attempt actually carried out or someone physically tested. No global or earlier tenter verb exists. Prepare the desire-arousing meaning under proper French tenter, without inventing a separate participial lemma. All four masculine singular predicates fit il est; inclination rather than prevention or deterrence selects tenté. The character’s suspicion does not verify supernatural powers.

items.meaning: take for; regard as
items.reviewNote: Prendre pour des sorciers means regarding the philosophers as sorcerers, often mistaken identification. The exact charge/trick surface banks and the global regard-as meaning with all three prise questions were read. Add the infinitive on the existing proper prendre regard-as sense. The alternatives are grammatical verb labels in a construction-identification prompt; identify-as rather than separation, distinction or protection selects prendre. The pour route in package02 remains paired with this exact semantic construction before import.

items.meaning: sorcerers; people believed to use magic
items.reviewNote: Sorciers names the supposed magical practitioners in the Saturnian’s tentative interpretation of human knowledge. No global or earlier proper sorcier noun exists. Sorciers/savants/artisans/médecins are masculine plural nouns after des; attributed magical power differs from study, craft or medical practice. The bank explains the character’s suspicion without asserting magic as real or classifying the philosophers as actual sorcerers.

items.meaning: same; the identical people previously mentioned
items.reviewNote: Ces mêmes gens resumes exactly those people who had earlier been denied souls, emphasizing the reversal in the Saturnian’s judgment. The global same, identical and emphatic-identity meanings, and the exact mêmes postposed bank, were read. Add this preposed-identity bank on the existing broad proper adjective same sense; whole-family overlap reconciliation must preserve old mastery before import. All alternatives agree with plural personnes; the clue selects identity over difference or novelty.

items.meaning: to whom; to which people or things
items.reviewNote: Auxquels resumes gens as recipients of the Saturnian’s earlier refusal of a soul. The global proper contracted-relative owner and all three auquel questions were read. Add the masculine plural form on that same à+lequel meaning, without an animate-only or plural-only sense. All options are grammatical pronoun labels in the metalinguistic prompt; à contraction rather than de, bare relative or demonstrative reference selects auxquels.

items.meaning: had; auxiliary forming a completed past
items.reviewNote: Il avait refusé forms a completed earlier action, not possession. The published lexical avait bank and the global compound auxiliary’s full three-band bank were read. Add this imperfect singular surface on that existing proper avoir auxiliary meaning; tense does not create a fresh sense. Alternatives are viable verb labels in the metalinguistic prompt, and auxiliary function selects avait. The lexical possession in211 and existential il y avait in210 are routed separately.

items.meaning: there was; existed in il y avait
items.reviewNote: Il y avait là un petit animalcule presents the existence or presence of another philosopher. The global existential avoir meaning and its three questions were read, excluding lexical possession and compound auxiliary. Add the imperfect surface on the same proper avoir existential sense; retain the indispensable y component and earlier IV missing-y repair dependency before import. All four singular predicates accept il y and a following subject; existence differs from remaining, passing or disappearance.

items.meaning: denied; refused to grant or acknowledge
items.reviewNote: Refusé une âme means denying or refusing to acknowledge a soul in the human philosophers. No global or earlier French refuser verb exists. Every participle fits le leur a; withholding rather than granting, recognizing or promising selects refusé. Keep the source’s philosophical denial rather than claim that souls are material objects or that the denial is true.

items.meaning: soul; the supposed principle of life and thought
items.reviewNote: All eight âme uses concern the philosophers’ proposed principle of life and thought, contrasted with body or matter. Académie1762 records the animating and thinking principle; the existing moral/affective inner-self sense and all three banks were read. Prepare the philosophical life/thought scope under the same proper âme noun, with explicit overlap reconciliation of inner-self and philosophical soul before import. Âme/idée/image/illusion are feminine singular vowel-initial nouns fitting l’; the proposed animating principle differs from a thought, representation or deception. No assertion of its existence or of one philosophical theory’s correctness is made.

items.meaning: quarter; one of four equal parts
items.reviewNote: Un quart d’heure is a quarter of an hour, not a navigational quadrant or an angular instrument. The global fraction meaning and all three quarts questions were read. Add the singular surface on that same proper noun fraction sense, without a time-only or number-only meaning. Quart/demi/tiers/cinquième are masculine singular fractional nouns; a four-part denominator selects quart.

items.meaning: before; previously
items.reviewNote: Auparavant locates the denial of a soul earlier and compares the later simultaneous speech with previous speech. No global or earlier French auparavant adverb exists. All four adverbs are viable time labels in the unchanged prompt; earlier rather than later, present or future time selects auparavant. Comparison with previous speech does not create a separate comparison-only sense.

items.meaning: even; strengthening a comparison
items.reviewNote: Encore mieux intensifies the comparative, meaning even better, rather than merely continuing to know. The global comparative encore/encor meaning and all three historical-form questions were read, as was the exact generic continuation bank. Add the modern surface on the same proper encore comparative sense; spelling does not create a new meaning. All four alternatives are grammatical adverb labels in the metalinguistic prompt; additional comparative degree differs from approximation, earlier time or low frequency.

items.meaning: form; create or shape in the mind
items.reviewNote: Formez vos idées asks how thoughts are formed, not self-cultivation se former l’esprit or things coming into being under se former. The earlier I cultivation and V formation proposals and their banks were read. Prepare this intentional creation/shaping meaning under the same proper planned former verb, with overlap reconciliation of mental cultivation and composition before import, rather than a new lemma. All four plural verbs take les; producing an idea differs from forgetting, rejecting or concealing it.

items.meaning: spoke; expressed themselves through speech
items.reviewNote: Parlèrent describes all philosophers speaking together. The published parler speech definition and all three parlé questions, plus VI parla/parlaient banks, were read. Add the past plural surface to the same proper French parler speech meaning, with no tense-only identity and no implication that their simultaneous answers agreed. Each plural predicate fits ils; spoken expression differs from writing, sleep or singing.

items.meaning: opinions; views on a question
items.reviewNote: Différents avis are plural opinions, not notices posted publicly. The existing opinion meaning and three exact avis questions were read; its middle noun alternatives were singular. Author a plural-context bank on the same invariant surface and same opinion meaning: avis/projets/voyages/récits are masculine plural nouns. Before import reconcile shared-bank selection and every current/historical dependent avis question, preserving old mastery; plurality does not create a fresh sense or identity.

items.meaning: the older man; the oldest man in this group
items.reviewNote: Le plus vieux names the oldest philosopher directly, while un vieux péripatéticien and le vieux secrétaire remain adjective uses. The global old adjective owner and all three questions were read; no proper nominal owner exists. Académie1798 explicitly records vieux as a substantive. Prepare substantive vieux under its own French noun ownership, while comparing the age concept before import. Vieux/jeune/enfant/adolescent are masculine singular substantive noun labels in the metalinguistic prompt, avoiding a superlative construction that would reject distractors by syntax. Do not create separate old-versus-oldest noun meanings.

items.meaning: cited; quoted or invoked an author as authority
items.reviewNote: Citait Aristote names quoting or invoking Aristotle’s writings as authority; the following speech quotes a purported passage. No global or earlier French citer verb exists. All singular imperfect predicates accept le; citing as support differs from disregard, rejection or criticism. The bank does not verify the attributed quotation, page reference or the speaker’s understanding of the text.

items.meaning: pronounced; said aloud
items.reviewNote: Prononçait le nom de Descartes is saying a name aloud, not issuing a judicial decision or a phonetic-correctness judgment. The earlier VI prononça speech bank and all three questions were read. Add the imperfect form to the same planned proper prononcer meaning, with no name-only or tense-only sense. All four singular predicates take les; utterance differs from writing, erasing or forgetting.

items.meaning: Peripatetic; a follower of Aristotle’s philosophy
items.reviewNote: Un vieux péripatéticien directly names a follower of Aristotle, rather than an adjective modifying a separate philosopher noun. No global or earlier proper péripatéticien owner exists. Académie9 records this masculine noun and its separate adjectival use. Péripatéticien/cartésien/leibnitzien/lockien are masculine singular philosophical-follower nouns; the named doctrine selects the target, without validating the character’s alleged Aristotelian quotation.

items.meaning: confidence; assurance in what one says
items.reviewNote: Avec confiance describes the peripatetic speaker’s assurance, not financial credit or necessarily trust placed in another person. No global or earlier proper confiance noun exists. Confiance/hésitation/incertitude/méfiance are feminine singular nouns after avec, with no elision filter. Assurance differs from hesitation, uncertainty or distrust; being confident does not establish that the assertion is true.

items.meaning: entelechy; the essential form or realized principle of a being
items.reviewNote: The peripatetic calls the soul une entéléchie. Académie1762 explains essential form constituting an individual and directing organized beings to their ends; Académie9 records completed actuality, contrasted with an act in progress. Use the historical essential-form/realized-principle scope for this passage, not merely latent potentiality. No global or earlier French owner exists. Entéléchie/matière/possibilité/apparence are feminine singular noun labels; essential constitution differs from raw material, mere possibility or superficial appearance. This gloss does not endorse the speaker’s supposed Aristotle quotation.

items.meaning: reason; an explanatory principle or ground
items.reviewNote: Une raison par qui elle a la puissance d’être is presented by the speaker as an explanatory ground, not the faculty of rational thought, having right judgment or state interest. This contextual reading is an editorial inference from the sentence, supported by Académie’s cause/motive/explanation usage, and does not certify the attributed Aristotle wording. The published rationale, generic reason and earlier IV grounds banks were read. Add an explanatory-ground bank on the same proper rationale noun sense; before import reconcile its current action-focused definition with explanation of an entity and examine every current/historical dependent bank. Raison/conséquence/apparence/interdiction are feminine singular nouns after une; foundation differs from result, appearance or prohibition.

items.meaning: expressly; explicitly and clearly
items.reviewNote: Déclare expressément marks the peripatetic’s claim that Aristotle stated this explicitly. No global or earlier French expressément adverb exists. All four adverbs fit the authored declaration frame; explicit formulation differs from vagueness, implication or silence. The bank explains manner of statement, not a verified claim about Aristotle or the cited edition.
